newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-News shares sag in U.S. on Heritage deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-News shares sag in U.S. on Heritage deal.

text.p: Shares in media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd sagged on Monday as investors questioned the company's $1.35 billion stock-and-debt deal to buy Heritage Media Corp.
News Corp preferred American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) fell 7/8 to 17 and its ordinary ADRs fell 5/8 to 20-1/4. Trade in both was moderate.

Heritage Media, the United States' biggest provider of in-store marketing services and the owner of radio and television stations, jumped 6-1/8 to 18-1/4 in very heavy trade. Analysts said the acquisition of such Heritage units as ACTMEDIA that provide products like coupons to drug stores and supermarkets were a good fit for News Corp's free-standing inserts (FSI) business.
However, they questioned Murdoch's further investment in inserts and the effect News Corp's continuing buying spree would have on its balance sheet.

In the last year or so News Corp has spent about $5 billion on purchases, including the $2.8 billion acquisition of New World Communications Group Inc. Most of the purchases have been paid for with stock.
"Strategically it's good; from an earnings standpoint it's good," said Andrew Melinek, head of ADR research and sales at NatWest Securities.
Under the deal, News Corp would pay the equivalent of $20.50 for each of Heritage's 38.6 million shares, or a total of $754 million, by issuing preferred limited voting ordinary ADRs.
News Corp also will assume about $600 million in outstanding debt.
"The problem is Murdoch spending $1.3 billion," Melinek said. "... It's back to more spending and that has disappointed the market."
Richard Read, an analyst with Arnhold & Bleichroeder, said, "My reaction is that I would rather see the investment elsewhere than FSI and related areas."
Added Ed Hatch, an analyst at UBS Securities, "Strategically (Heritage Media) is an excellent fit to its direct marketing business."
Heritage also owns six television stations and 24 radio stations and News Corp said it would sell all of them. Their value was not immediately known.
